output.title: What seasonality can hide in a small business workflow
output.body:
Seasonality can hide a simple problem: the work that keeps repeating even when sales go up and down.

If you run a small business, don’t start by asking, “How do I automate seasonality?” Start by asking which one workflow stays there all year. It might be repeated customer questions, invoice or data handling, or another task that returns every week or month. The season changes the volume. It does not always change the workflow.

That is the useful diagnostic. List 2–3 recurring tasks, then pick the one with the clearest output. Look for a task where you can say what “correct” means: a clean handoff, a checked field, a sent reply, or an approved record. If you cannot define that, it is probably too fuzzy for a small automation.

Bareni’s rule is plain: if the task is repetitive, has a measurable input and output, and still matters outside peak season, it is worth a closer look. If it disappears for months, or if the “correct” answer depends on judgment you do not want to delegate, leave it manual.

The practical next step is a free 30-minute diagnostic. Map the workflow end to end, check where the seasonal noise is, and decide whether AI plus a small automation tool could return a human-approved output. No drama; just the work on paper first.
